subject: MATH
title: Mathematics 7
description: Grade 7 mathematics centered on proportional reasoning, operations with rational numbers, expressions and equations, geometry of scale, circles, angles, area, surface area and volume, and probability and sampling. The sequence mirrors the Illustrative Mathematics Grade 7 scope used by many California districts, with rich tasks, number talks, and real-world modeling aligned to the 2023 CA Mathematics Framework's big ideas.
framework: California Common Core State Standards for Mathematics; 2023 CA Mathematics Framework

standards.7.RP.A.1: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas and other quantities.
standards.7.RP.A.2: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.
standards.7.RP.A.2a: Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship using tables or graphs through the origin.
standards.7.RP.A.2b: Identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in tables, graphs, equations, diagrams and verbal descriptions.
standards.7.RP.A.2c: Represent proportional relationships by equations such as y = kx.
standards.7.RP.A.2d: Explain what a point (x, y) on the graph of a proportional relationship means, including (0,0) and (1, r).
standards.7.RP.A.3: Use proportional relationships to solve multistep ratio and percent problems (tax, tips, markups, discounts, interest, percent error).
standards.7.NS.A.1: Apply and extend understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers; represent on a number line.
standards.7.NS.A.2: Apply and extend understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide rational numbers.
standards.7.NS.A.2d: Convert a rational number to a decimal using long division; know it terminates or repeats.
standards.7.NS.A.3: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with rational numbers.
standards.7.EE.A.1: Apply properties of operations to add, subtract, factor and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.
standards.7.EE.A.2: Understand that rewriting an expression in different forms can shed light on how quantities are related.
standards.7.EE.B.3: Solve multistep real-life problems with positive and negative rational numbers in any form; assess reasonableness with estimation.
standards.7.EE.B.4: Use variables to represent quantities and construct simple equations and inequalities to solve problems.
standards.7.EE.B.4a: Solve word problems leading to equations px + q = r and p(x + q) = r fluently; compare algebraic and arithmetic solutions.
standards.7.EE.B.4b: Solve word problems leading to inequalities px + q > r or px + q < r; graph and interpret the solution set.
standards.7.G.A.1: Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures, including computing actual lengths and areas and reproducing a drawing at a different scale.
standards.7.G.A.2: Draw geometric shapes with given conditions; construct triangles from three measures of angles or sides and note when a unique triangle results.
standards.7.G.A.3: Describe the two-dimensional figures that result from slicing three-dimensional figures.
standards.7.G.B.4: Know and use the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle; give an informal derivation of the relationship.
standards.7.G.B.5: Use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical and adjacent angles to write and solve equations for an unknown angle.
standards.7.G.B.6: Solve real-world problems involving area, volume and surface area of 2-D and 3-D objects composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, cubes and right prisms.
standards.7.SP.A.1: Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by examining a representative sample; random sampling.
standards.7.SP.A.2: Use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population; gauge variation in estimates from multiple samples.
standards.7.SP.B.3: Informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical data distributions with similar variabilities.
standards.7.SP.B.4: Use measures of center and variability from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.
standards.7.SP.C.5: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 expressing likelihood.
standards.7.SP.C.6: Approximate the probability of a chance event by collecting data and observing long-run relative frequency.
standards.7.SP.C.7: Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of events; compare to observed frequencies.
standards.7.SP.C.8: Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams and simulation.

units.title: Scale Drawings
units.big_idea: Scaled copies keep angles and multiply every length by the same scale factor; areas scale by the square of the factor.

units.title: Introducing Proportional Relationships
units.big_idea: A proportional relationship has a constant of proportionality that appears in tables, equations y = kx and graphs through the origin.

units.title: Measuring Circles
units.big_idea: Circumference is proportional to diameter with constant pi; area of a circle is pi r squared.

units.title: Proportional Relationships and Percentages
units.big_idea: Percent change, tax, tips, discounts, interest and error are all proportional reasoning.

units.title: Rational Number Arithmetic
units.big_idea: Positive and negative numbers obey consistent rules for all four operations, modeled with number lines and real contexts.

units.title: Expressions, Equations, and Inequalities
units.big_idea: Equivalent expressions and balanced equations let us solve for unknowns; inequalities describe ranges of solutions.

units.title: Angles, Triangles, and Prisms
units.big_idea: Angle relationships produce equations; triangles are determined by certain measures; prisms have measurable surface area and volume.

units.title: Probability and Sampling
units.big_idea: Probability measures likelihood; random samples let us make inferences and compare populations.

objectives: Distinguish scaled copies from non-scaled copies
Find corresponding parts and scale factors

days.title: Pre-assessment & math autobiography
days.work: Take a 20-question grade 6 readiness check (ratios, fractions, decimals, area) and write a half-page math autobiography describing strengths and goals.

days.title: Scaled copies
days.work: Compare five versions of a letter 'F' drawn on grid paper and decide which are scaled copies, explaining which lengths changed and how.

days.title: Corresponding parts
days.work: Label corresponding points, segments and angles on pairs of polygons; measure angles with a protractor to see that angles stay the same.

days.title: Making scaled copies
days.work: Draw a scaled copy of a grid polygon with scale factor 3, then 1/2, and write how each side length changed.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a 6-problem quiz identifying scale factors and drawing a scaled copy; correct mistakes in a different color.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on scale factor and scaled-copy drawing; readiness check used to plan review.

objectives: Use scale factors to find unknown lengths
Explain how area changes by the square of the scale factor

days.title: Finding scale factors
days.work: Find the scale factor between pairs of figures, including factors less than 1, and use them to compute missing side lengths.

days.title: Reversing a scale
days.work: Scale a triangle up by 4 then back down by 1/4 and explain why the reciprocal undoes the scaling.

days.title: Scaling area
days.work: Build squares and triangles from pattern blocks at scale factors 2 and 3, count pieces, and record that area grows by 4 and 9.

days.title: Area problems
days.work: Solve 8 problems finding the area of scaled rectangles and triangles from the original area and scale factor.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on scale factor, reciprocal scaling and area scaling with one written explanation.

weeks.assessment: Quiz and written explanation of why area scales by the square of the factor.

objectives: Use scales with units to find actual distances
Convert between scales with and without units

days.title: Reading a scale
days.work: Use the scale 1 cm to 50 km on a California map to find road distances between five cities.

days.title: Creating a scale drawing
days.work: Measure a bedroom or kitchen with a tape measure and plan a scale drawing using 1 inch to 2 feet.

days.title: Scales without units
days.work: Rewrite scales like 1 in to 10 ft as 1 to 120 and compare which of two map scales shows more detail.

days.title: Equivalent scales
days.work: Decide which of six scales are equivalent and redraw a basketball court at a new scale.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Finish the room floor plan in scale with labeled actual dimensions and answer 5 map distance questions.

weeks.assessment: Floor-plan scale drawing scored with a rubric (accuracy, labels, scale) plus map quiz.

objectives: Apply scale to a real design

days.title: Dream space design
days.work: Design a dream classroom or park at a chosen scale, listing at least six objects with actual and scaled dimensions.

days.title: Actual area
days.work: Compute actual area of each region in the design using the scale and record in a table.

days.title: Redraw at new scale
days.work: Redraw one part of the design at half the original scale and compare the two drawings' areas.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Work a mixed review set of 12 problems on scaled copies, scale factor, maps and area.

days.title: Unit 1 test
days.work: Take the unit 1 test and present the design poster aloud, explaining how the scale was used.

weeks.assessment: Unit 1 test and scale design project.

days.title: One of these things
days.work: Compare recipes for lemonade that taste the same versus different and organize the amounts in tables.

days.title: Constant of proportionality
days.work: Find k in tables of cost versus pounds and miles versus hours, writing k as a unit rate with units.

days.title: Both directions
days.work: Find the constant of proportionality from x to y and y to x in a currency-conversion table and note they are reciprocals.

days.title: Not proportional
days.work: Sort 8 tables into proportional and not proportional, explaining with ratios that are or are not equivalent.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: identify proportional tables, find k, and fill in missing table values.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on tables and constant of proportionality.

objectives: Compute unit rates from ratios of fractions

days.title: Walking rates
days.work: Time how long it takes to walk 1/4 mile and compute miles per hour using a ratio of fractions.

days.title: Complex fractions
days.work: Simplify complex fractions like (1/2)/(3/4) by multiplying by the reciprocal and connect to unit rate.

days.title: Recipe rates
days.work: Find cups of flour per batch and batches per cup from a recipe using 2/3 cup for 1/2 batch.

days.title: Area rates
days.work: Find how much paint covers 1 square yard if 1/3 gallon covers 2 1/2 square yards; solve 6 similar problems.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a 10-problem fraction unit-rate set and correct errors.

weeks.assessment: Problem set on unit rates with fractions.

objectives: Write equations of form y = kx

days.title: From table to equation
days.work: Write y = kx equations for tables of gas cost, hourly pay and unit price taken from real receipts.

days.title: Using equations
days.work: Use y = 3.25x to answer forward and backward questions about cost and quantity.

days.title: Two equations
days.work: Write both y = kx and x = (1/k)y for a recipe and explain what each tells you.

days.title: Proportional or not?
days.work: Decide whether equations like y = 4x, y = x + 4 and y = 4/x are proportional and justify with tables.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz writing and using equations for proportional relationships.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on writing and interpreting y = kx.

days.title: Graphing tables
days.work: Graph three tables on the coordinate plane and identify which form straight lines through the origin.

days.title: Meaning of points
days.work: Explain what (0,0), (1,k) and (5,y) mean on a graph of distance versus time for a cyclist.

days.title: Comparing graphs
days.work: Graph two runners' distance-time lines on Desmos and decide who is faster using the constant of proportionality.

days.title: Four representations
days.work: Complete a card match linking descriptions, tables, equations and graphs for six relationships.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz interpreting points and steepness on proportional graphs.

days.title: Collecting data
days.work: Measure how much water drips from a faucet in 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 minutes and record in a table.

days.title: Modeling
days.work: Graph the drip data, find k, write an equation, and predict water wasted in a day and a year.

days.title: Report
days.work: Write a one-page report explaining whether the relationship is proportional and what the constant means.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Complete a mixed review on tables, equations, graphs and unit rates with fractions.

days.title: Unit 2 test
days.work: Take the unit 2 test covering all representations of proportional relationships.

weeks.assessment: Unit 2 test and dripping-faucet modeling report.

objectives: Discover pi as the ratio of circumference to diameter
materials: cans and lids of different sizes

days.title: Parts of a circle
days.work: Use a compass to draw circles and label center, radius, diameter and circumference; note d = 2r.

days.title: Measuring around
days.work: Measure diameter and circumference of 6 household circles with string, record in a table and graph circumference versus diameter.

days.title: Discovering pi
days.work: Compute C/d for each object, average the ratios, and compare to 3.14 and 22/7.

days.title: Applying circumference
days.work: Solve problems such as how far a bike wheel travels in 10 rotations and finding diameter from circumference.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on circle vocabulary, C = pi d and C = 2 pi r.

weeks.assessment: Measurement lab table and circumference quiz.

days.title: Estimating area
days.work: Trace a circle on grid paper and estimate its area by counting squares, comparing to r squared.

days.title: Cutting the circle
days.work: Cut a paper plate into 16 sectors and rearrange them into a near-parallelogram to show area is pi r times r.

days.title: Using the formula
days.work: Find areas of pizzas, sprinkler regions and circular gardens given radius or diameter.

days.title: Area vs circumference
days.work: Decide whether 8 situations need area or circumference (fencing vs sod, crust vs cheese) and solve each.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on area of circles and choosing the correct measure.

weeks.assessment: Quiz and written derivation explaining the plate rearrangement.

objectives: Find areas and perimeters of composite shapes with circles

days.title: Semicircles and quarters
days.work: Find perimeter and area of semicircles and quarter circles, including the straight edges.

days.title: Composite figures
days.work: Find areas of a running track shape and a window shaped like a rectangle topped with a semicircle.

days.title: Expressing in terms of pi
days.work: Write answers both as exact expressions with pi and as decimal approximations and compare.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Solve a review set of 10 problems on circumference, area and composite shapes.

days.title: Unit 3 test
days.work: Take the unit 3 test on circles.

objectives: Represent percent change with tape diagrams and equations

days.title: Lots of fractions
days.work: Use tape diagrams to show 1/4 more and 1/4 less than a quantity and connect to 125% and 75%.

days.title: Percent increase
days.work: Compute new prices after increases of 10%, 15% and 120% using multiplication by 1.10, 1.15 and 2.20.

days.title: Percent decrease
days.work: Compute sale prices after discounts and find the original price given the sale price.

days.title: Finding percent change
days.work: Find percent change from old to new values for populations, prices and test scores.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on percent increase and decrease with tape diagrams and equations.

objectives: Use percent equations in shopping contexts

days.title: Sales tax
days.work: Compute California sales tax (use local rate) on five purchases and find the tax rate from a receipt.

days.title: Tips
days.work: Compute 15%, 18% and 20% tips on menu orders using mental math (10% then adjust).

days.title: Markup and markdown
days.work: Solve problems where a store marks up wholesale cost by 40% then discounts the retail price by 25%.

days.title: Commission and fees
days.work: Calculate salesperson commission and service fees, then solve 'which deal is better' comparisons.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Plan a restaurant meal for a family within $60 including tax and tip and show all calculations.

weeks.assessment: Restaurant budget task and short quiz.

days.title: Simple interest
days.work: Compute simple interest on savings and loans using I = Prt for different rates and years.

days.title: Comparing accounts
days.work: Compare two savings accounts and one loan in a table and decide which is best for a goal.

days.title: Percent error lab
days.work: Estimate the masses of 5 objects, weigh them on a kitchen scale, and compute percent error for each estimate.

days.title: Error and tolerance
days.work: Solve problems about manufacturing tolerance, e.g., a 500 g bag allowed 2% error.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on simple interest and percent error.

objectives: Apply percent reasoning to a budget

days.title: Shopping project
days.work: Choose a $200 back-to-school budget and select items from ads, applying discounts and coupons.

days.title: Adding tax
days.work: Add sales tax, compute total savings as a percent of original price, and adjust to stay within budget.

days.title: Presentation
days.work: Create a one-page receipt-style summary showing every calculation and the percent saved.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Mixed review of percent change, tax, tips, interest and error.

days.title: Unit 4 test
days.work: Take the unit 4 test on percentages.

weeks.topic: Positive and negative numbers; adding rational numbers
objectives: Add integers and rational numbers on a number line

days.title: Interpreting negatives
days.work: Describe temperatures, elevations and bank balances with signed numbers and order them on a number line.

days.title: Adding with arrows
days.work: Model sums such as -5 + 8 and 3 + (-7) with arrows on a number line and with two-color counters.

days.title: Zero pairs
days.work: Use zero pairs to explain why a number plus its opposite is 0 and solve 12 addition problems.

days.title: Adding fractions and decimals

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on adding rational numbers in context.

objectives: Understand subtraction as adding the opposite
Find distance between numbers as absolute value of difference

days.title: Subtracting with counters
days.work: Model 3 - 5 and -2 - (-6) with counters, adding zero pairs when needed.

days.title: Add the opposite
days.work: Rewrite 15 subtraction problems as addition of the opposite and solve.

days.title: Distance
days.work: Find distances between elevations like Death Valley (-282 ft) and Mt. Whitney (14,505 ft) using |a - b|.

days.title: Changes in temperature
days.work: Compute temperature changes over a week from a weather table and graph them.

days.title: Semester review & check
days.work: Take a cumulative semester 1 checkpoint covering units 1–5 so far.

days.title: Position and velocity
days.work: Model multiplication with a toy car moving at positive or negative velocities for positive or negative time.

days.title: Sign patterns
days.work: Complete a multiplication table from -5 to 5 and describe the patterns that produce the sign rules.

days.title: Distributive reasoning
days.work: Use -3(4 + -4) = 0 to justify why -3 times -4 must equal positive 12.

days.title: Fractions and decimals
days.work: Multiply 15 signed fraction and decimal problems including multiple factors.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on multiplying rational numbers.

weeks.assessment: Multiplication quiz and written justification of sign rules.

objectives: Convert fractions to terminating or repeating decimals

days.title: Dividing signed numbers
days.work: Use multiplication facts to determine sign rules for division and solve 15 division problems.

days.title: Dividing by zero
days.work: Explore why division by zero is undefined using related multiplication sentences and write an explanation.

days.title: Long division to decimals
days.work: Convert 1/8, 3/11, 5/6 and 7/16 to decimals by long division and mark repeating parts with bar notation.

days.title: Which fractions terminate?
days.work: Investigate which denominators give terminating decimals and state a rule based on factors of 2 and 5.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on division and fraction-to-decimal conversion.

weeks.topic: Four operations with rational numbers in context
objectives: Solve multistep problems with rational numbers

days.work: Track a month of deposits and withdrawals in a check register using signed decimals.

days.title: Order of operations

days.title: Rate problems
days.work: Solve problems about a diver descending at -1.5 m/s and a tank draining at -2.25 gal/min.

days.title: Estimation
days.work: Estimate answers to 8 multistep problems before solving and compare estimate to exact answer.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on multistep rational-number problems.

objectives: Apply rational number operations to solving equations

days.title: Solving simple equations
days.work: Solve one-step equations with negative numbers like x + 4.5 = -2 and -3x = 18.

days.title: Representing contexts
days.work: Write and solve equations for situations involving temperature drops and debt.

days.title: Game day
days.work: Play an integer card game (red = negative, black = positive) for sums and products and record 20 rounds.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Mixed review of all four operations with rational numbers.

days.title: Unit 5 test
days.work: Take the unit 5 test on rational number arithmetic.

objectives: Write equations p(x + q) = r and px + q = r

days.title: Relationships and diagrams
days.work: Match 6 stories to tape diagrams showing px + q = r or p(x + q) = r.

days.title: Writing equations
days.work: Write equations for situations such as 4 friends each buying a $2.50 snack plus a shared $6 pizza.

days.title: Hanger diagrams
days.work: Use balanced hanger diagrams to reason about solving 3x + 2 = 11.

days.title: Solving with balance
days.work: Solve 10 equations by doing the same to each side and checking solutions.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on writing equations from diagrams and stories.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on tape diagrams and equation writing.

objectives: Solve px + q = r and p(x + q) = r fluently

days.title: Two methods
days.work: Solve 2(x + 3) = 14 by dividing first and by distributing first, comparing steps.

days.title: Negative coefficients
days.work: Solve equations with negative and fractional coefficients like -2/3 x + 5 = -7.

days.title: Word problems
days.work: Solve 8 word problems leading to two-step equations and check reasonableness.

days.title: Arithmetic vs algebra
days.work: Solve a problem by working backward arithmetically and by equation, then write which made more sense and why.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on two-step equations.

objectives: Solve and interpret px + q > r

days.title: Representing situations
days.work: Write inequalities for situations like 'at least 13 to ride' and graph them on number lines.

days.title: Finding solutions
days.work: Test values in inequalities and discover the reverse when multiplying or dividing by a negative.

days.title: Solving inequalities
days.work: Solve 10 inequalities like 5x - 3 ≥ 22 and -2x + 4 < 10 and graph the solutions.

days.title: Inequalities in context

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on writing, solving and graphing inequalities.

days.title: Subtraction in expressions
days.work: Rewrite expressions with subtraction as adding the opposite and evaluate to test equivalence.

days.title: Distributive property
days.work: Expand and factor expressions like 6(2x - 5) and 12x + 18 using area models.

days.title: Combining like terms
days.work: Simplify expressions such as 3x - 4 - 7x + 2.5 and check by substituting values.

days.title: Rewriting for meaning
days.work: Explain why 'increase by 5%' can be written as a + 0.05a or 1.05a and solve 4 similar problems.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on equivalent expressions.

objectives: Model real problems with expressions, equations and inequalities

days.title: Visual patterns
days.work: Write expressions for the nth step of two visual patterns and show the expressions are equivalent.

days.title: Fundraiser problem

days.title: Phone plans

days.title: Unit 6 test

objectives: Identify complementary, supplementary, vertical and adjacent angles
Write and solve equations for unknown angles

weeks.topic: Cross sections and volume of prisms

objectives: Describe probability as a number from 0 to 1

objectives: Compare two populations with measures of center and variability

days.work: Take 5 random samples of 10 words, compare sample means and describe the variability.

days.title: Comparing groups
days.work: Compare two dot plots (e.g., heights of two plant groups) using means and MAD and decide if the difference is meaningful.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on sampling and comparing populations.

weeks.assessment: Sampling quiz and word-length sampling report.

days.title: Plan an investigation
days.work: Write a statistical question comparing two groups (e.g., reaction times of kids vs adults) and plan a random sample.

days.title: Collect and display
days.work: Collect data from at least 10 people per group with a ruler-drop test and create dot plots or box plots.

days.title: Analyze and report
days.work: Compute means and MADs, write conclusions, and present findings to the family.

days.title: Final review
days.work: Complete a cumulative review covering all 8 units.

days.title: Final exam
days.work: Take the year-end grade 7 math exam and set goals for Math 8.

weeks.assessment: Final exam and statistics investigation report.
